And he arose immediately.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="35">35 And all that dwelt at <ns0:note n="e" place="bottom">Verse 32.</ns0:note> Lydda, and <ns0:note n="f" place="bottom">
                     <ns0:hi>Saron</ns0:hi> is the name of a City, 1 <ns0:hi>Chron.</ns0:hi> 5.16. but here it is rather the name of a Countrey, (which the masculine article usually shews) lying between Mount <ns0:hi>Tha<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />bor,</ns0:hi> and the Lake of <ns0:hi>Tiberias,</ns0:hi> a very-fruitful plain, 1 <ns0:hi>Chron.</ns0:hi> 27.29. <ns0:hi>Cant.</ns0:hi> 2. To the owning of his truth. Error (if in fundamentals) keeps us from God.</ns0:note> Saron, saw him, and turned to the Lord.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="36">36 ¶ Now there was at <ns0:note n="g" place="bottom">A post-town, see <ns0:hi>Chap.</ns0:hi> 10.5. These circumstances of places and persons, are set down to evidence the certainty of the History.</ns0:note> Joppa a certain disci<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ple named <ns0:note n="h" place="bottom">
                     <ns0:hi>Tabitha,</ns0:hi> according to the <ns0:hi>Syriack</ns0:hi> dialect then in use amongst the <ns0:hi>Iews,</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Dorcas</ns0:hi> as <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>he was called among the <ns0:hi>Greeks</ns0:hi>; it being common for the same person to have two names, one <ns0:hi>Hebrew</ns0:hi> and the other <ns0:hi>Greek,</ns0:hi> as <ns0:hi>Thomas</ns0:hi> who was called <ns0:hi>Didymus,</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Cephas</ns0:hi> who was called <ns0:hi>Peter.</ns0:hi>
                  </ns0:note> Tabitha, which by interpretation is called Dorcas: this woman was <ns0:note n="i" place="bottom">She was rich in good works, which are the best riches, last longest, and go farthest.</ns0:note> full of good works, and alms deeds which she did.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="37">37 And it came to pass in those days, that she was sick, and died: whom when they had <ns0:note n="k" place="bottom">They washed the dead, and anointed them, to fit them for their burying, and especially to shew their hope of the Resurrection; which some think St. <ns0:hi>Paul</ns0:hi> alludes unto, 1 <ns0:hi>Cor.</ns0:hi> 15.29.</ns0:note> wash<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ed, they laid <ns0:hi>her</ns0:hi> in an upper chamber.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="38">38 And forasmuch as Lydda was nigh to Joppa, and the disciples had heard that Peter was there, they sent <ns0:note n="l" place="bottom">They sent for <ns0:hi>Peter,</ns0:hi> that he might come to comfort those that were concerned in the great loss of so good a woman, and it may be not without some hopes of her re<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />covery by a Miracle from St. <ns0:hi>Peter</ns0:hi>; which is the likelier, because they so much hasten his coming to them.</ns0:note> unto him two men, de<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />siring <ns0:hi>him</ns0:hi> that he would not <ns0:note n="m" place="bottom">She be<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ing already dead, and they preparing for her burial.</ns0:note> 
                  <ns0:note n="‖" place="margin">Or, <ns0:hi>be grie<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ved.</ns0:hi>
                  </ns0:note> delay to come to them.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="39">39 <ns0:note n="n" place="bottom">It was strange that <ns0:hi>Peter</ns0:hi> should be sent for, or that he should go on such an account, <ns0:hi>viz.</ns0:hi> to raise one that was dead; but God, who had ordered this Miracle for the manifestation of his truth and glory, so wrought in their hearts, that they did this out of faith; tho if others should think to imitate it, it would be but presumption.</ns0:note> Then Peter arose and went with them. When he was come, they brought him into the upper chamber: and all the widows stood by him <ns0:note n="o" place="bottom">Here needed no mourning women to be hired; the death of this good woman was a common loss: these coats were made by <ns0:hi>Dorcas</ns0:hi> in her life time, to cloath the poor and naked with all.</ns0:note> weeping, and shewing the coats and gar<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ments which Dorcas made while she was with them.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="40">40 But Peter <ns0:note n="p" place="bottom">
                     <ns0:hi>Peter</ns0:hi> put them out, that he might pray the more ear<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />nestly, without distraction, or interruption; thus <ns0:hi>Elisha</ns0:hi> shut the door to him, 2 <ns0:hi>Kings</ns0:hi> 4.33 when he prayed for the <ns0:hi>Shunamites</ns0:hi> Son.</ns0:note> put them all forth, and <ns0:note n="q" place="bottom">This his kneeling is mentioned, to recommend reverence in our praying unto God.</ns0:note> kneeled down <ns0:note n="r" place="bottom">
                     <ns0:hi>Peter</ns0:hi> by his betaking himself unto Prayer, would shew, that he could do nothing by his own power, but it must co<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>e from above; and he had every mercy, as much preca<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>iously, and by prayer, as any other.</ns0:note> and prayed, and turning <ns0:hi>him</ns0:hi> to the body, said, Tabitha, arise. And she opened her eyes: and when she saw Peter, she sat up.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="41">41 And he gave her his hand, and lift her up; and when he had called <ns0:note n="s" place="bottom">Such who had sent for him, and now were gathered together, to see what effects his prayers might have.</ns0:note> the saints and widows, presented <ns0:note n="t" place="bottom">And in perfect health, as all were that were miraculously cured; for the Lords works are perfect. <ns0:hi>Deut.</ns0:hi> 32.4.</ns0:note> her alive.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="42">42 And it was known throughout all Joppa; and <ns0:note n="u" place="bottom">This cure was wrought, and all the other Miracles were done, to be a means to make the Gospel to be be<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />lieved, which he published, and was an undeniable proof, that this Doctrine was from Heaven; for none could do such things, unless God were with him, or rather unless God did them by him; So that this Miracle wrought by St. <ns0:hi>Peter,</ns0:hi> did more good to the Souls of many, than to the body of this relieved woman.</ns0:note> many believed in the Lord.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="43">43 And it came to pass, that he tarried <ns0:note n="x" place="bottom">The Miracle had onely prepared them to receive his Doctrine, which <ns0:hi>Peter</ns0:hi> tarried some time with them, to instruct them in: The Miracle had prepared the ground, and now he takes this season to sow the seed of the word into it.</ns0:note> many days in Joppa with one Simon a tan<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ner.</ns0:p>
